page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The server provides 48 dedicated physical cores via AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processors clocked at 2.6 GHz, operating at a single thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Bundled directly onto the instance is 2,850 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, complemented by a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier memory and multi-threaded throughput. The instance scored within the top 10% on PassMark memory testing, driven by uncached read bandwidth reaching 274.85 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 116.34 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is robust, ranking in the top 25% across stress-ng multi-core (73,467.4), Geekbench multi-core (19,220.0), and Clang compilation (50,958.0). Single-core operations in Geekbench (1,518.0) and stress-ng (1,533.09) exhibit middle-tier performance, reflecting balanced per-core clock rates rather than extreme single-thread frequency peaks.

Data handling and web throughput demonstrate significant capability, with Redis SET operations achieving 76.38 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measuring 65.01 GB/sec. PassMark database operations also place in the top 25%. However, without discrete hardware accelerators, large language model text generation remains modest, delivering 4.23 tokens per second on 70B parameter models.

Given its high core count, low memory-to-core overhead, and large integrated NVMe storage volume, the c7gd.12xlarge delivers solid resource efficiency for high-concurrency tasks. It is well configured for continuous integration and software compilation pipelines, distributed caching layers, batch data processing, high-volume web serving, and database instances requiring fast ephemeral storage.
